categories.name: repo-metadata
categories.rationale: Top-level files that describe the public repository itself. README, LICENSE, third-party notices, package manifest, gitignore and workspace file are WRITTEN FOR THE PUBLIC TREE under scripts/public-export/public-tree/ and mapped to the root by pathMap — they are not copies of the private root files, which carry dead script targets and a private sibling-repository reference. tsconfig.base.json is the real base config both published tsconfigs extend. The verify-apnt skill is NOT here — it verifies proofs and trusted descriptors, so it ships with them under verifier-surface (v0.2), not with repo identity (v0.1); see that category's rationale.

categories.name: spec
categories.rationale: Promoted OpenSpec capability specifications. These are normative requirement documents with no private material: they describe what the protocol must do, not any key, seed or live wallet. Console and Ligero capabilities are excluded by rule; the transition-and-conservation spec is withheld because its requirement text names private witness fields.

categories.name: protocol-runtime
categories.rationale: A partial, import-closed, strict-clean subset of @bch-cloak/protocol-runtime: pure protocol objects, byte and serialization primitives, commitment hashing, note trees, transition statements, seals and projections, plus the CashAssembly covenant sources. The set has ZERO external npm dependencies and every relative import inside it resolves within the published tree. Its package barrel and package.json are deliberately NOT published, because modules they re-export were withheld and shipping them would claim a package that does not exist here.

categories.name: chain-io
categories.rationale: @bch-cloak/chain-io in full: the Fulcrum/Electrum client used to read chain state. Both sources, its tsconfig and its manifest. It has no workspace dependencies and imports only Node builtins. It is published complete rather than partially, including the UNSAFE_TRANSPARENT_UTXO_FIELDS_V0 scrubber that keeps private field names out of transparent UTXO records. Four of its five test files are published so that the build gate's `pnpm -r test` leg exercises something real rather than matching zero files; each imports only ../src/index.js, node builtins and vitest, and their only network endpoint is a 127.0.0.1 fixture.

categories.name: verifier-surface
categories.rationale: The verification surface: the canonical Groth16 proof artifacts, the quotient/residue certificate runs, the frozen trusted verifier descriptors, the Rust note-commitment verifier crate, and THREE independent Node checkers — one grading certificate-run keying, one re-deriving statementCommitment32 and settlementProjection32 from published statement bytes, one re-deriving the settlement-authorization covenant's bytes and L_verdict. All three run on a bare Node with no install, no network and no build, and the export executes all four configured argument sets inside a filesystem-sandboxed copy of the staged tree before this tree may ship. Their two data inputs are derived, not copied: typescript-golden-vectors-public-v0.json is emitted by derive-public-golden-vectors-v0.mjs, which strips the private witness and refuses to write unless six redaction proofs pass; apnt-settlement-authorization-covenant-bytecode-v0.json is emitted by the landed covenant builders and carries only on-chain script bytes. The verify-apnt skill ships here rather than under repo-metadata: it walks a contributor through checking a proof artifact, a settlement, a note commitment and a trust anchor, so it belongs with the artifacts it teaches a reader to check, not with repo identity that ships before any of them exist.
